Chlorine is prepared by action of Manganese(IV) oxide, $\mathrm{MnO_2}$, on concentrated Hydrochloric acid.

(i) State the specific role of $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ in the reaction.

(ii) Write an equation for the reaction. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ is the **oxidising agent**. It oxidises the chloride ions of the hydrochloric acid to chlorine gas, and is itself reduced (manganese goes from oxidation state $+4$ in $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ to $+2$ in $\mathrm{MnCl_2}$). It is not a catalyst, because it is used up in the reaction.

(ii) The mixture is gently heated:

$$
\mathrm{MnO_2 + 4HCl \rightarrow MnCl_2 + Cl_2 + 2H_2O}
$$

Check, atom by atom: Mn 1 = 1; O 2 = 2; H 4 = 4; Cl 4 = 2 + 2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
When Bromine is bubbled through colourless Potassium iodide solution, the following reaction occurs:

$\mathrm{Br_2(l) + 2KI(aq) \rightarrow 2KBr(aq) + I_2(s)}$

(i) State one colour change likely to occur during the reaction.

(ii) Suggest what you think would happen if $\mathrm{I_2}$ vapour is bubbled into $\mathrm{KBr(aq)}$. Explain.

Suggestion: ........

Reason: ........ *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The **colourless** potassium iodide solution turns **brown** (yellow-brown) because iodine, $\mathrm{I_2}$, is formed. (The orange-brown colour of the bromine also fades as it is used up.)

(ii) **Suggestion:** nothing happens; there is **no reaction** (no colour change, no bromine formed).

**Reason:** iodine is **less reactive** than bromine. A halogen displaces from a solution of its salt only a halogen that is *below* it in reactivity. The reactivity of the halogens decreases down the group (Cl > Br > I), so iodine cannot displace bromine from potassium bromide:

$$
\mathrm{I_2 + 2KBr \rightarrow \text{no reaction}}
$$
